title: Edge resilience VPC onboarding cheat sheet
summary: Compact operational playbook for onboarding customers that require VPC + edge resiliency patterns (hybrid on-prem + region-backed fallbacks). Focused on terraform module decisions, cutover checklist, upgrade & rollback criteria, and observability hooks.
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a compact, ops-focused cheat sheet we can hand to Solutions/SE during customer kickoff for VPC-onboarding projects where the customer expects: local on‑prem endpoint(s) + cloud region fallback, predictable failover, and terraform-driven deployment. It is intentionally terse — use this alongside the longer playbooks (link above).

Audience:
- Solutions/SE running kickoff with network/security teams
- Private Deployments engineers doing implementation and upgrades
- Release engineers planning terraform module changes or state migrations

Core design goals (for this class of onboarding)
1) Fast failure detection and deterministic failover (3–15s target for critical inference path).
2) Minimal blast radius during upgrades — per-tenant & per-edge canary strategies.
3) Clear operational ownership for routes, NAT/egress, and cert rotation.
4) Terraform-first provisioning: use modules that decouple tenant networking from infra plane.

High-level reference architecture (textual):
- Customer edge (on-prem appliance or hosted customer gateway) -> BGP peering or GRE -> Transit VPC in customer account (if cloud) / Transit network at colocation for crossconnects.
- Transit VPC -> Regional inference VPC (Redwood-managed/private tenant VPC) with private endpoints for control plane + model endpoints.
- Active-active region pairs for critical workloads; local on-prem preferred for low latency with automatic fallback to closest region.
- Observability: packet traces to S3 / ELK for flow capture; per-route latency histograms and TTL-based health probes.

Minimal terraform module pattern (opinions):
- modules/vpc-edge (creates transit attachments, route propagation, NAT gateways, route tables)
- modules/peering (BGP config, ASN assignment, prefix filters as variables)
- modules/edge-operator (bootstrap service account, IAM roles for cross-account peering, cert resources)
- modules/tfstate-bridge (for migrating TF state when moving from customer-managed to redwood-managed modules)

Example variables for modules/vpc-edge (copy into onboarding template):
- var.customer_name = "acme-corp"
- var.edge_location = "dc-chi1"
- var.onprem_prefixes = ["10.200.0.0/22"]
- var.bgp_asn = 65050
- var.failover_regions = ["us-west-2", "us-east-1"]
- var-egress_mode = "centralized"   # centralized | distributed

Upgrade and canary plan (high level):
1) Prep: run infra-lint and drift check, verify module inputs, generate plan and post to PR with cost delta.
2) Preflight: run network acceptance tests in staging (see Acceptance tests below).
3) Canary (edge-level): roll module changes to a single edge location with synthetic traffic and doubled latencies to simulate failover. Hold for 60–120m.
4) Canary (tenant-level): choose one low-risk tenant, deploy with traffic mirroring for 1h, verify metrics.
5) Gradual rollout by region/edge, increase to full roll within 24–72h depending on customer SLA.
6) Post-upgrade validation and telemetry review.

Rollback criteria (immediate rollback triggers):
- Error rate on inference API > 2.5x baseline for > 5 minutes.
- Latency P95 increased > 40% and sustained for 10 minutes.
- Route flapping observed in BGP sessions > 3 resets within 15 minutes.
- Any cert/key rotation failures preventing control-plane operations.

Cutover checklist (quick):
- [ ] Confirm customer has provided peering IPs, ASN and contact window.
- [ ] Verify shared routes and prefix filters; lock down broad 0.0.0.0/0 leaks.
- [ ] Confirm KMS key policies for any cross-account encryption are in place.
- [ ] Ensure Terraform state backend with locking configured.
- [ ] Validate lb health checks and path-based probes for model endpoints.
- [ ] Run synthetic smoke tests from on-prem -> edge -> inference VPC.
- [ ] Confirm monitoring dashboards have tenant-level filters and alerts.

Acceptance tests (automated):
- Connectivity: TCP handshake and BGP session established for 3 consecutive 1-minute checks.
- Data path: 100 synthetic inference requests at 10 qps, P50 < 40ms on local edge, failover simulation sees < 200ms increase within 10s.
- Cert rotation: force rotation in staging and verify both old+new certs accepted during TTL.
- Negative tests: introduce a blackhole route and validate failover occurs and reverts when resolved.

Observability and SLO hooks:
- Export per-tenant route latency histograms to Grafana; create alert if median latency deviates by >20% post-deploy.
- Tag flows with tenant_id and edge_location to enable rapid RCA.
- Keep 7-day raw packet capture retention for customer incidents, 90-day aggregated metrics.

Security and compliance notes (quick hits):
- Egress filtering: prefer centralized egress to customer-managed NAT where regulatory egress logging is required.
- Key management: customer-managed KMS recommended for PII workloads; require explicit KMS key alias and ARNs at kickoff.
- Audit: enable VPC Flow Logs (ingress/egress) and forward to customer SIEM if requested.

Common pitfalls & gotchas observed in past onboards:
- Customer expects symmetric routing but only configures one BGP session -> leads to asymmetric paths and intermittent timeouts.
- Terraform modules with implicit resource names cause state collisions during multiple tenant deployments; use unique prefixes.
- NAT gateway quotas exceeded when scaling multiple edges in a single AZ — recommend using egress NAT per-edge as fallback.
- Certificate chain issues when customers terminate TLS at the edge and expect mutual TLS with Redwood control-plane.

Rollforward plan for terraform module changes that affect networking primitives:
- Create feature branch and module version bump.
- Publish module to internal registry with both vX and vX+1 available.
- Update a single staging tenant module ref and validate.
- Communicate planned sr windows to SRE and support on Slack (#private-onboards).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide on default for var-egress_mode across regulated vs non-regulated customers (Ethan to propose by 2024-11-10).
- Add a small Terraform helper that validates BGP prefix filters before apply (owner: Luca).
- Formalize the post-cutover telemetry checklist into a dashboard template (Maya to draft).

References & links:
- Onboarding template PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/178
- Network acceptance tests harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/net-tests
- Related Confluence guide: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/VPC+Reference+Patterns

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this short; customers hate 30-page docs during kickoff. Use diagrams in Confluence and hand them the cheat sheet.
- For high-risk customers, schedule a test failover window during low-traffic hours.

--- end of cheat sheet ---

Unresolved: should we include a mandatory pre-onboard security questionnaire (list of 12 items)? I think yes for regulated tenants; add as appendix to onboarding template.
